title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and a translation vector of zero, zero, and zero. On the first face, draw the first loop consisting of four lines: the first line starts at the origin and ends at coordinates (0.0266, 0.0); the second line starts at (0.0266, 0.0) and ends at (0.0266, 0.0696); the third line starts at (0.0266, 0.0696) and ends at (0.0, 0.0696); and the fourth line starts at (0.0, 0.0696) and returns to the origin. Scale the two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.0696. Rotate the scaled two-dimensional sketch using the same Euler angles and translate it using the same translation vector. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch along its normal by 0.75 units, ensuring no extrusion in the opposite direction. Create a new solid body from this extrusion. The dimensions of the final shape are a length of 0.0266 units, a width of 0.0696 units, and a height of 0.75 units. The final shape is a cylindrical object with a rectangular section at one end.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0266, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0266, 0.0696) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0696) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are -90.0, 0.0, -90.0 and the translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
